newsitem.title: ANGOLA: Angola army boosts presence in Cabinda - diplomats.
newsitem.headline: Angola army boosts presence in Cabinda - diplomats.

text.p: The Angolan army is increasing its military presence in the oil-rich Cabinda enclave bordering Zaire but the reason for the buildup is not clear, Western diplomats said on Wednesday.
"There has been a marked military buildup in Cabinda lately," one Western diplomat told Reuters.
"But it is not certain what they are doing there. It is likely these troops will be used against domestic insurgents but they might be preparing to move into Zairean territory," the diplomat added.
Cabinda, separated from the rest of Angola by a thin strip of Zairean territory and the Zaire river, is about 400 km (250 miles) west of Kinshasa.
Separatist FLEC guerrillas, fighting for the independence of the enclave, have bases in Zaire and the Angolan government has said it plans to step up military action against them.
Angola has consistently denied any involvement in backing Laurent Kabila's rebels who have seized most of Zaire in their fight to topple President Mobutu Sese Seko.
But Mobutu's government and independent military analysts say Angolan armour is involved in the rebels' march towards Zaire's capital, Kinshasa.

The two countries have never been at war, but during Angola's long civil war Zaire harboured UNITA guerrillas opposed to the Luanda government, and Angola took Katangese gendarme forces after their revolt against Mobutu failed.
A South African political analyst on Angola told Reuters Mobutu had warned the Angolan government that if it continued to back the rebels in Zaire he would target Cabinda's oil installations.
These produce more than 60 percent of the country's entire oil production, worth nearly $4 billion annually, and rank fourth in the world as suppliers to the United States.
"Mr Mobutu sent a very clear message in April to the Angolans saying if they continued to back Kabila in Zaire he would point his rockets at the oil installations in Cabinda," the analyst said.

Foreign companies operating in Cabinda, including the U.S. Chevron oil corporation, sought an urgent meeting with Angola's military commanders in Cabinda on April 26 where they expressed concern over their investments after reports that Angolan troops had crossed into Zaire from Cabinda.
"I would be surprised if the Angolans really invade (Zaire)," another diplomat in Luanda said.
"But you can certainly expect them to use this time to take out those FLEC bases in Zaire," the diplomat added.

Oil company officials in Cabinda say however there is no visible increase in the presence of Angolan troops, which could be hard to detect in the thick jungles. Pilots flying in the area also say they have seen no unusual military activity.

But military analysts told Reuters there had been heavy troops movement by the Angolan army from the Cabo Ledo coastal military base, south of Luanda, to Saurimo in the diamond-rich Lunda Sul province in the northeast, close to the Zaire border.

The Cabo Ledo base was previously used by the Pretoria-based Executive Outcomes company to train Angolan government troops during the last years of the country's 20-year civil war which ended in 1994.
